evals.prompt: Define a React Server Component in 2-3 sentences. Name what it can do that a Client Component cannot, what it cannot do, and how its output reaches the browser.
expected_elements: Runs only on the server, never ships to the browser as JavaScript, can be async
Can directly access server-side resources (databases, file system, secrets, server-only env vars)
Cannot use state, effects, event handlers, or browser APIs (those are Client Component territory)
Output is serialized to the RSC payload and reconstituted into the client tree without a separate API layer

evals.prompt: Explain the directionality rule between Server and Client Components, and how a Server Component can still appear 'inside' a Client Component.
expected_elements: A Server Component can render/import a Client Component, but a Client Component cannot import a Server Component
Reason: the client bundler would have to bundle the Server Component, violating the no-ship rule
A Client Component CAN receive a Server Component as a children/slot prop (already-rendered content from the parent)
The children prop is content, not components-to-import

evals.prompt: Why is the disciplined boundary 'use client at the interactive leaves' rather than at the page level? What is the cost of marking the whole page 'use client'?
expected_elements: Marking the whole page 'use client' loses all RSC benefit
Ships the entire page as a client bundle and re-runs every component on hydration
Thinnest-client-boundary: 'use client' belongs at the smallest leaf that genuinely needs state/effects/handlers/browser APIs
The surrounding layout, data reads, and non-interactive structure stay on the server (zero bundle, no hydration)

evals.prompt: A Server Component does <Profile user={userRow} /> where userRow is a full database row but <Profile> only shows the name. What is wrong and how do you fix it? Name the guards.
expected_elements: Every prop crossing to a Client Component is serialized into the RSC payload and shipped to the browser — including fields never rendered
The full row (password hash, internal flags, every column) is now visible in browser devtools — a leak
Primary fix: filter to a minimal DTO before crossing (return only public fields the client needs)
Backstops: a server-only Data Access Layer (authorization + DTOs), the server-only package, and the React taint APIs

evals.prompt: How should an interactive Client Component get slow data fetched on the server without using useEffect and without blocking the whole subtree? Describe the use() Promise-handoff pattern and its two safety rules.
expected_elements: Start the query in the Server Component, pass the unawaited Promise as a prop, unwrap it in the Client Component with use()
A Promise is a serializable prop in React 19+; use() suspends until it resolves under a Suspense boundary
Rule 1: create the Promise on the server, never freshly during the Client Component's render (a new Promise each render re-suspends forever)
Rule 2: the Suspense boundary catching the suspension must sit above the component calling use()

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the server-components-design skill to design the form-submission mutation flow with 'use server' functions and re-authorization inside the action. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Not in scope — that is server-actions-design (the write path: mutations, 'use server' functions, re-authorization inside the action)
server-components-design owns the read path (components that fetch and render data)
They share the server/client boundary infrastructure but are disjoint design surfaces
Correctly redirects rather than answering the mutation-design question out of lane

evals.prompt: A developer says: 'I'll mark this file use client just to be safe, and I still need /api/data to fetch the rows.' Correct both mental models.
expected_elements: 'use client' to be safe is wrong — default is Server; a component is Client only because a forcing requirement (hook/handler/browser API) forced it
A same-app /api/data route is not needed for Server Component reads — query the database directly from the Server Component
An API route is only needed when something OUTSIDE the app reads the data (mobile app, third-party integration, server-to-server)
Calling fetch('/api/...') against your own app turns an in-process read into a wasteful HTTP round-trip and can fail at build

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify a Server Components tree is designed correctly? Cover the boundary, data security, and freshness/streaming dimensions.
expected_elements: 'use client' is at the thinnest interactive leaf, not higher; import direction is valid (no Client Component imports a Server Component)
No Client Component prop carries more data than it renders — whole rows are filtered to DTOs; secret/DB modules guarded with server-only
Privileged reads authenticate AND authorize (resource ownership); raw request inputs (params/searchParams/cookies/headers) are not trusted as permission signals and are awaited, read low in the tree

Independent reads run in parallel (siblings/Promise.all), shared reads deduped with React.cache(); slow reads wrapped in co-located Suspense; each read has a named freshness strategy (uncached / React cache / framework 'use cache' / external)

evals.prompt: Why are params, searchParams, cookies(), and headers() async in the current App Router, and what two design rules follow from reading them?
expected_elements: They are async so the framework can start streaming the shell before resolving request inputs (synchronous inputs would block streaming)
Rule 1: read them as low in the tree as possible — any component reading a request input is dynamic; reading high (root layout) taints the whole subtree as dynamic and loses prerendering/caching
Rule 2: none of the four is a trust signal — params/searchParams/headers are user-controlled and forgeable; re-verify the real session server-side
?isAdmin=true proves nothing; gate authorization on a verified session and resource ownership, not raw request input
